We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{\infty }\frac{3}{{\theta }^{3}}\,\text{d}\theta  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{a}\frac{3}{{\theta }^{3}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{1}^{a}3{\theta }^{-3}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={lim}_{a\to \infty }{[(-\frac{3}{2}{\theta }^{-2})]}_{1}^{a} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[\frac{1}{{\theta }^{2}}]}_{1}^{a} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }(\frac{1}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{1}{{1}^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}(0-1) \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
